ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within a square grid with side length 1, points A, B, and C are on grid points, and lines AB and CD intersect at point D. What is the value of $\sin \angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend CD to meet another vertex of the square at $E$, and connect BE, as shown in the diagram:\\
From the problem statement, it is known that: $\angle BED=90^\circ$, $\angle ADC=\angle BDE$,\\
Based on the side length of the small square grid and the Pythagorean theorem, it can be derived that: $BE=2\sqrt{2}$, $BD=\sqrt{10}$,\\
$\therefore$ In $\triangle BDE$, $\sin\angle BDE=\frac{BE}{BD}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\
$\therefore \sin\angle ADC=\sin\angle BDE=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

method.method_draft: Use slopes and the angle-between-lines formula. From the image, line CD rises 1 square for every 1 square horizontally, so its slope is m_CD=1. Line AB, as seen through D and B, drops 1 square over 3 squares to the right, so its slope is m_AB=-1/3. The angle ADC is the angle between these two lines, so tan theta=|(m_CD-m_AB)/(1+m_CD*m_AB)|=|(1-(-1/3))/(1-1/3)|=2. Therefore sin theta=tan theta/sqrt(1+tan^2 theta)=2/sqrt(5)=2sqrt(5)/5.
